questions.q: Which metric most directly measures how long it takes a new engineer to make their first meaningful contribution using the platform?
options: Developer onboarding time
Total number of Kubernetes clusters in production
Lines of Terraform code written per sprint
Platform team headcount
questions.explain: Developer onboarding time is a direct read on whether the platform's promised cognitive-load reduction is real. If a new hire still needs weeks of tribal-knowledge conversations to ship anything, the self-service layer isn't doing its job.

questions.q: What does "time-to-first-deploy" measure, and why does it matter for evaluating a platform?
options: How many deploys happen per quarter company-wide
How long the CI pipeline takes to run unit tests in isolation
The uptime percentage of the production environment
The elapsed time from a developer starting a new service to it successfully reaching production, which reflects how well the golden path removes friction
questions.explain: This metric is sensitive to exactly the friction a golden path should remove — provisioning delays, unclear pipeline setup, review bottlenecks. A working platform should make it shrink predictably over time.

questions.q: Why does golden-path adoption rate matter as a platform metric, beyond simply showing developers are using it?
options: It has no real diagnostic value as a metric
A low adoption rate, even when the golden path is technically available, signals the path doesn't fit real needs yet or isn't trusted — the same failure mode a mandate can hide
It only matters for internal billing and cost allocation
It measures how many support tickets the help desk closed that week
questions.explain: Golden-path adoption rate catches exactly the gap Lesson 2 warned about: a platform that's mandatory in name can still be avoided in practice. Low adoption is a direct signal to investigate, not a vanity number.

questions.q: What should a platform team do with onboarding time, time-to-first-deploy, and adoption metrics, according to this lesson?
options: Report them only to external auditors and otherwise ignore them
Delete them periodically to avoid internal scrutiny
Use them the way a product team uses usage data — to decide what to build or fix next on the roadmap
Treat them as fixed facts that can't be improved once the platform has shipped
questions.explain: These metrics only pay off if they drive action: a spike in time-to-first-deploy points at a specific bottleneck to fix, and low golden-path adoption calls for investigation rather than a louder mandate.

questions.q: Which of these does this lesson explicitly identify as NOT a sufficient measure of whether a platform is succeeding?
options: Golden-path adoption rate
Time-to-first-deploy trends
Developer satisfaction survey trends over time
System uptime alone, with no view into developer experience or real adoption
questions.explain: A platform can have excellent uptime and still be failing if teams have quietly stopped routing real work through it. Uptime measures reliability, not whether anyone is actually choosing to use the platform.
